span.label: existence
span.quote: But the interference of conflicting word stimuli upon the time for naming 100 colors (each color being the print of a word which names another color) caused an increase of 47.0 seconds or 74.3 percent of the normal time for naming colors printed in squares.

span.label: color-word interference
span.quote: Interference in serial verbal reactions has been studied by means of newly devised experimental materials.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: Seventy college undergraduates (14 males and 56 females) were used as subjects.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: interference from automaticity: the highly-practiced automatic response (reading a word) competes with a slower, less-automatic response (naming the ink color), so conflicting color words slow color naming - the Stroop effect
span.quote: a given association can function automatically even though some effect of a previous contrary association remains

span.label: in one condition (reading incongruently-colored color names) the observed difference was not statistically reliable
span.note: what this limits: the reading-incongruent condition specifically: THIS DIFFERENCE IS NOT RELIABLE, WHICH IS IN AGREEMENT WITH PETERSON'S PREDICTION MADE WHEN THE TEST WAS FIRST PROPOSED
span.quote: This difference is not reliable which is in agreement with Peterson's prediction made when the test was first proposed.

span.label: The scheme used to penalise uncorrected errors was chosen arbitrarily rather than derived from an objective measure.
span.note: what this limits: every reported time: THIS PLAN OF CORRECTION WAS ARBITRARY BUT SEEMED TO BE JUSTIFIED BY THE SITUATION
span.quote: This plan of correction was arbitrary but seemed to be justified by the situation.

span.label: No accurate objective correction for uncorrected errors was available.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1, with the reason: SINCE NO ACCURATE OBJECTIVE MEASURE WAS OBTAINABLE AND THE NUMBER OF ERRORS WAS SMALL THE ARBITRARY PLAN WAS ADOPTED
span.quote: Since no accurate objective measure was obtainable and the number of errors was small the arbitrary plan was adopted.

span.label: Only the first two college-year groups had enough cases to support comparison.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison across college years: ONLY COLLEGE YEARS ONE AND TWO CONTAIN A SUFFICIENT NUMBER OF CASES FOR COMPARATIVE PURPOSES
span.quote: Only college years one and two contain a sufficient number of cases for comparative purposes.

span.label: the colour order constructed so that no colour repeats consecutively in a row or column, and each appears TWICE in every row and column
span.quote: The colors were arranged so as to avoid any regularity of occurrence and so that each color would appear twice in each column and in each row

span.label: interference
span.quote: The difference in the time for naming the colors in which the words are printed and the same colors printed in squares (or swastikas) is the measure of the interference of conflicting word stimuli upon naming colors

span.label: word stimuli
span.quote: the interference of conflicting word stimuli upon the time for naming 100 colors (each color being the print of a word which names another color) caused an increase of 47.0 seconds or 74.3 percent of the normal time for naming colors printed in squares

span.label: color stimuli
span.quote: The interference of conflicting color stimuli upon the time for reading 100 words (each word naming a color unlike the ink-color of its print) caused an increase of only 2.3 seconds or 5.6 percent over the normal time for reading the same words printed in black. This increase is not reliable

span.label: training
span.quote: since the difference in their strength corresponds roughly to the difference in training in reading words and naming colors, it seems reasonable to conclude that the difference in speed in reading names of colors and in naming colors may be satisfactorily accounted for by the difference in training in the two activities

span.label: practice
span.quote: The variability of the group is increased by the increase in interference due to practice on the NCWd test

span.label: **THE ASYMMETRY WITH BOTH HALVES, WHICH IS THE FINDING - NOT THE HALF THAT GETS QUOTED:** `The interference of conflicting color stimuli upon the time for reading 100 words ... caused an increase of ONLY 2.3 SECONDS OR 5.6 PERCENT over the normal time for reading the same words printed in black. THIS INCREASE IS NOT RELIABLE. But the interference of conflicting word stimuli upon the time for naming 100 colors ... caused an increase of 47.0 SECONDS OR 74.3 PERCENT.` **One direction is a null and the other is enormous.** A record that holds only `colour-word interference` has half of this paper; the whole of it is that interference runs one way and not the other, and that fact is what needs explaining
span.quote: The interference of conflicting color stimuli upon the time for reading 100 words (each word naming a color unlike the ink-color of its print) caused an increase of only 2.3 seconds or 5.6 percent over the normal time for reading the same words printed in black. This increase is not reliable. But the interference of conflicting word stimuli upon the time for naming 100 colors (each color being the print of a word which names another color) caused an increase of 47.0 seconds or 74.3 percent of the normal time for naming colors printed in squares

span.label: **AND STROOP'S EXPLANATION IS A TRAINING HISTORY, NOT AN ARCHITECTURE:** `The word stimulus has been associated with the SPECIFIC response 'to read,' while the color stimulus has been associated with VARIOUS responses: 'to admire,' 'to name,' 'to reach for,' 'to avoid,' etc.` **One-to-one against one-to-many.** Not automaticity, not a module, not a race between pathways - a difference in how many responses each stimulus class has been attached to over a lifetime. **It is in the paper's own SUMMARY, not buried in a discussion** - and because it is a claim about learning rather than about structure, it is testable by training, which is exactly what Stroop then does in Experiment 3. (An earlier version of this note said the training account is 'the part later citation usually loses'. I had not measured that and cannot from one record: the corpus holds 7 records mentioning Stroop, which is no base for 'usually', and counting how often those records say 'automatic' measures their own topics rather than what they attribute to him. Retracted 2026-08-19, Q-805)
span.quote: The word stimulus has been associated with the specific response 'to read,' while the color stimulus has been associated with various responses: 'to admire,' 'to name,' 'to reach for,' 'to avoid,' etc

span.label: **AND HE TESTED IT THE ONLY WAY THAT COULD SETTLE IT - BY TRAINING THE NULL DIRECTION UNTIL IT STOPPED BEING NULL.** Eight days, 200 reactions a day, naming the colours of conflicting words: `1. It DECREASED the interference of conflicting word stimuli to naming colors BUT DID NOT ELIMINATE IT. ... 5. It INCREASED THE INTERFERENCE OF CONFLICTING COLOR STIMULI UPON READING WORDS.` **The direction that was `not reliable` became reliable once it was trained**, and the direction that was enormous shrank. That is the training account making a prediction and collecting it, and it is stronger evidence than the headline asymmetry it explains
span.quote: It decreased the interference of conflicting word stimuli to naming colors but did not eliminate it. 2. It produced a practice curve comparable to that obtained in many other learning experiments. 3. It increased the variability of the group. 4. It shortened the reaction time to colors presented in color squares. 5. It increased the interference of conflicting color stimuli upon reading words

span.label: **AND THE INTERFERENCE HE BUILT DECAYED FASTER THAN THE ONE HE FOUND, WHICH IS A SEPARATE CLAIM:** `it is evident that the newly developed interference DISAPPEARS VERY RAPIDLY with practice. From one day to the next the mean decreases from 34.8 to 22.0 seconds. This indicates that RENEWING the effectiveness of OLD associations which are being opposed by newly formed ones is EASIER than STRENGTHENING NEW associations in opposition to old well established ones.` A trained interference is real but shallow; the lifetime one is not. **Age of an association, not just its strength** - and it is measured here in 1935 with a stopwatch
span.quote: it is evident that the newly developed interference disappears very rapidly with practice. From one day to the next the mean decreases from 34.8 to 22.0 seconds. This indicates that renewing the effectiveness of old associations which are being opposed by newly formed ones is easier than strengthening new associations in opposition to old well established ones

span.label: builds-on → prior experimental research on interference and inhibition
span.quote: Interference or inhibition (the terms seem to have been used almost indiscriminately) has been given a large place in experimental literature.

span.label: replicates → Woodworth-Wells (1911), Brown (1915) and Ligon (1932) on the sex difference in colour naming
span.quote: This reliable sex-difference favoring the females in naming colors agrees with the findings of Woodworth-Wells (1911), Brown (1915), Ligon (1932), etc.

span.label: builds-on → Peterson and Barlow's (1928) hypothesis about practice and individual differences
span.quote: These findings lend some support to Peterson's hypothesis, "Subjects of normal heterogeneity would become more alike with practice on the simpler processes or activities, but more different on the more complex activities" (Peterson and Barlow, 1928, p. 228).

span.label: builds-on → Peterson's prediction about the reading of colour names printed in conflicting colours
span.quote: This difference is not reliable which is in agreement with Peterson's prediction made when the test was first proposed.

span.label: word stimuli —causes→ interference
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.95 — THE EFFECT THE PAPER IS REMEMBERED FOR, at 4.35 standard deviation units. Weight 0.95: the number, the comparison condition and the reliability are all in the paper's own summary. **The edge that matters is the OTHER one** - this one alone is the half-quoted version.
span.quote: the interference of conflicting word stimuli upon the time for naming 100 colors (each color being the print of a word which names another color) caused an increase of 47.0 seconds or 74.3 percent of the normal time for naming colors printed in squares

span.label: color stimuli —causes→ interference
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.95 — **`no-change` ON A 5.6 PERCENT INCREASE, BECAUSE STROOP SAYS `THIS INCREASE IS NOT RELIABLE` AND THAT SENTENCE IS INSIDE THE QUOTE.** The point estimate is positive; the paper declines to treat it as an effect. Recording it as `increases` because the number is above zero would contradict the author, and dropping the edge would lose the half of the finding that needs explaining. **Read with the edge above, this pair IS the Stroop asymmetry** - and the third sense shows the null becoming reliable after eight days of training, which is what makes it a fact about learning rather than about colour.
span.quote: The interference of conflicting color stimuli upon the time for reading 100 words (each word naming a color unlike the ink-color of its print) caused an increase of only 2.3 seconds or 5.6 percent over the normal time for reading the same words printed in black. This increase is not reliable

span.label: practice —causes→ interference
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **THIS IS THE TRAINING ACCOUNT BEING COLLECTED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.** Eight days of naming the colours of conflicting words INCREASED the interference running the other way - the direction Experiment 1 had found `not reliable`. `due to` is Stroop's own attribution and it is in the quote. Weight 0.9: a measured within-subject change with the manipulation named, against 0.85 for the interpretive sentence where he says it `seems reasonable to conclude` that differential training explains the asymmetry. **The explanation is the `training` concept; this edge is the test of it.**
